summary: Mirza-ye Qomi was a Shiite jurist, mujtahid and religious reference. His birth name was Mirza Abolghasem Gilani. He lived during the reign of Fath Ali Shah Qajar. He belonged to the Usuli school. He was born in 1739 in Japelaq, Iran. His name comes from his residence in Qom. He first studied under his father. He then studied in Khansar under Seyyed Hossein Khansari. In 1761 he went to Iraq to study. Muhammad Baqir Behbahani granted him permission for ijtihad. He moved to Qom and soon headed its Shiite authority. Qom's seminary then overshadowed Isfahan's. Fath Ali Shah visited him and prayed behind him. He trained many prominent jurists and scholars. His most important work is Qawanin al-Usul, written in 1791. It was a key seminary textbook for over forty years. He also wrote Jameh al-Shatat, a book of legal answers. He wrote poetry in Persian and Arabic. He was also known for calligraphy. He died in 1815 and was buried in Qom.
